sources_opened.pages: PDF pp. 22, 33-38, 45, 55 (printed ch. A.1 pp. 6, 17-22, 29, 39): p. 21 shows Def. 3.8 satisfaction; p. 22 shows sentence/assignment independence, the substitution proviso, elementary equivalence and (finite) axiomatizability

components.note: All three listed subcomponents are supplied with written proofs; the original note (conservativity unproved in the example; Beth leans on it) is met: the example points to the theorem, which is stated with a complete proof on the active route (p02.tex lines 71 and 73; annex p02.tex line 36).

Relative definitional extension defined for a fresh relation symbol (R not in L; FV(phi) within pairwise distinct x1..xn; delta_R) and for a fresh function/constant symbol relative to T with the unique-value premise T|=Tot_phi and T|=Uni_phi; freshness and admissibility stated explicitly at body lines 378-380; parameter failure shown at lines 750-757.

Existence and uniqueness of the expansion proved for relations (inherited clause 1 with written proof; body corollary clause 1 for every L-structure, annex proof) and for function/constant symbols (fn-expansion clauses 1-3, annex proof written step by step); satisfaction translation theorems for psi* and psi# with written annex proofs by induction on complexity; invariance under reduct proved on route.

Conservativity over the original signature proved for relation symbols (inherited clause 2) and for function/constant symbols under the unique-value premise (fn-conservativity clause 2), with necessity of the premise (clause 4) and finite sequences of definitions; all proofs written in the annex; failure examples for dropped uniqueness/existence.
